rv.q: At the same time, their dependence on repetition and intentional naïveté starts to wear thin.
This piece would be timeless under normal circumstances, but with American boots on the ground in conflicts all over the world, now it’s downright chilling.
It's an approach one can call wide-ranging, which is apparently a Milo Cramer specialty.
There's plenty of talent on display here, and an appealing let's-put-on-a-show quality, but it's hard to sustain this much twee over an entire show.
Though No Singing in the Navy occasionally veers off-course, the heart at its center holds steady.
No Singing in the Navy is vacuous, an inside joke shared mainly by the author and himself.
